- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates in the first 5–10 days post-spike, then corrects downward — suggest smoothing or lagged response.
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts too low when recent history shows upward momentum, and too high when prices are falling.
- High forecast variance in early days (e.g., 1–3 days) — reduce volatility in initial forecast window.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, adjust next forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- If forecast is below 60% of historical mean for 5+ days, increase forecast by 1–3% to avoid underestimation bias.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day spikes — model should lag 1–2 days in response to price corrections.
